svg.title: Crowd coding: the path of a message through a shared room
svg.desc: A message from a participant passes the Google Chat access gate, the ChannelManager pause check, the ChannelTaskBridge steps (reserved commands, per-sender rate limit, bound-thread routing) and the MessageQueue before one shared-session turn. Facilitator commands, the pause queue and turn limits branch off the main path.
svg.text: Crowd coding: the path of a message through a shared room
Pause, reserved commands and the rate limit are decided before a message can reach a session or a task.

g.title: Participants write ordinary language in a Google Chat Space. Facilitators are the senders listed in governance.admin_senders; an empty list makes every sender an admin.
g.text: a trusted group in one Google Chat Space

g.title: Google Chat webhook (GoogleChatWebhookHandler). Runs the inbound gate: group_access and the group allowlist, then require_mention. A registered app command is answered here and never reaches the ChannelManager. A message that also arrives through Space Events is processed once.

ChannelManager.handleInboundMessage: finds the owning channel, derives the session key (group_scope: shared gives one session per space), looks up a task thread binding, then checks the pause flag. A paused, non-reserved message goes to the PauseController queue.
g.text: paused and not a reserved command: held in the queue

g.title: ChannelTaskBridge.tryHandle, in this order: 0 reserved command (consumed whether run or refused), 1 per-sender rate limit (admins and reserved commands exempt; the sender gets a rejection naming the limit), 2 bound-thread routing. The rate limit comes before bound-thread routing so a limited sender cannot bypass it inside a bound thread.
g.text: 2 bound thread: route to that task's session
a message consumed at 0, 1 or 2 stops here

g.title: MessageQueue: messages from one sender in one session inside the debounce window (1 s) are joined; one turn runs per session at a time. queue_strategy: fair rotates across senders so one participant cannot monopolize the shared session.
g.text: debounce 1 s, one turn per session at a time

g.title: dispatchChannelTurn: persist the message, start a primary-lane turn. Model and effort resolve from the allowlist row, sessions.channels, sessions, then governance.crowd_coding for group sessions, then the provider default. The agent calls registered MCP tools; the host parses no chat grammar.
g.text: one conversation shared by every participant

g.title: SlashCommandHandler. Google Chat app commands: /new <description> creates and starts a task, /reset starts a fresh shared session, /status reports state, /stop, /pause and /resume act as the reserved commands do and need an admin sender. They are handled in the webhook, after the access gate, so neither the pause queue nor the per-sender rate limit applies to them.
g.text: answered before the bridge: no rate limit applies

g.title: PauseController: in-memory, so it resets on restart. While paused, reserved commands still run and every other message is queued (capacity 200, plus governance.rate_limits.per_sender.max_pause_queued per sender, admins exempt). /resume drains the queue and unpauses in one step; messages are grouped by session and replayed as one "While paused, N participants sent messages" prompt.
g.text: /pause: new messages wait in an in-memory queue
/resume replays them as one prompt per session
max_pause_queued per sender; resets on restart

g.title: ReservedCommandHandler. Matches /stop (and stop!), /pause, /resume, /bind <task-id>, /unbind exactly. Non-admin senders are refused and one audit entry is written. /stop runs EmergencyStopHandler: cancels active turns and every running or queued task, and broadcasts an emergency_stop event.
g.text: /stop cancels active turns and running or queued tasks

g.title: Thread binding (features.thread_binding.enabled). A message in a thread bound to a live task is enqueued on that task's session instead of the shared session. Bindings are written by /bind, task_bind and the first task notification; they end when the task is terminal or after idle_timeout_minutes (default 60).
g.text: a bound thread routes straight to that task's session

g.title: governance limits that apply to every turn, whoever sent the message. rate_limits.global caps turn starts per window across all senders; budget.daily_tokens refuses new turns once spent (action: block) or only warns; loop_detection aborts or warns on runaway turns. Admin senders are not exempt from any of these three.
g.text: rate_limits.global: turns per window, all senders
budget: daily_tokens, action block or warn

g.title: The reply goes back into the Space, in the message's thread when it has one. Outbound text passes the redactor, then Google Chat formatting and chunking.
g.text: same Space, same thread when there is one

svg.text: data or control flow; numbers give the order of the main path
Opened directly in a browser, hovering a box highlights its outgoing arrows and shows its detail.
